title: Deep Learning for Time Series Forecasting: Advances and Open Problems
authors: Casolaro, A.; Capone, V.; Iannuzzo, G.; Camastra, F.
tldr: Comprehensive survey of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting covering short-term models (CNN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, GNN, GANs, Diffusion Models) and long-term models (Transformer variants) with benchmarking comparisons.
problem_and_motivation: Existing reviews on deep learning for time series forecasting lack coverage of Transformer variants, do not distinguish between short-term and long-term forecasting models, omit recent architectures like GNNs and Diffusion Models.
approach: Review categorizes architectures into short-term (CNN, TCN, RNN, LSTM, GRU, GNN, DGP, GANs, Diffusion Models) and long-term (Transformer and variants).
Survey scope restricted to works from 2016 onward for tractability.
Benchmarking section provides comparative results on standardized short-term (M4) and long-term (ETT, Electricity, Traffic, Weather, Exchange, ILI) data sets.
Architecture descriptions include formal mathematical definitions and application tables.
Transformer variants (Informer, Autoformer, FEDFormer, PatchTST, Crossformer, Pyraformer, Scaleformer, Triformer, Non-stationary Transformer) are reviewed.
findings: Vanilla RNNs suffer from vanishing/exploding gradients, limiting long-term dependency learning.
LSTM and GRU gated cells mitigate gradient instability but still struggle with very distant sequence dependencies.
Graph Neural Networks enable multivariate forecasting by modeling inter-variable relationships.
Deep Gaussian Processes provide confidence intervals for predictions, unlike most other deep learning architectures.
GANs serve two roles: data augmentation for small datasets and end-to-end generative forecasting models.
Diffusion models represent a new generative paradigm for probabilistic time series forecasting.
PatchTST achieves strong long-term forecasting by treating each variate as independent univariate series.
Non-stationary Transformer addresses the over-stationarization problem via Series Stationarization and De-stationary Attention.
Most deep learning forecasting architectures cannot estimate prediction confidence intervals.
Stationarity assumption violations cause concept drift, dramatically decreasing prediction accuracy.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Comprehensive survey of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, categorizing models by short-term and long-term horizons. Fills gaps by including Transformer-based models and presenting dedicated benchmarking comparisons. Four open problems identified: lack of confidence interval estimation, overfitting, data augmentation inadequacies, and non-stationarity handling.
directly_justifies: Deep learning applied to time series forecasting can cope with complex high-dimensional series.
Most deep learning methods except DGPs cannot estimate confidence intervals.
Vanilla RNNs suffer from vanishing or exploding gradients preventing long-term dependency learning.
PatchTST achieves competitive long-term forecasting by treating each dimension as independent univariate series.
Stationarity assumption violations lead to concept drift and dramatic accuracy decreases.
limits: Survey scope restricted to post-2016 works.
Spatio-temporal time series forecasting with GNNs explicitly excluded.
Benchmark comparisons rely on results reported in original papers rather than standardized re-evaluation.
Does not cover edge deployment or computational cost comparisons.

limitations: Survey restricted to works from 2016 onward.
Spatio-temporal forecasting with GNNs explicitly excluded despite relevance to multivariate financial data.
Benchmark comparisons rely on results reported in original papers, introducing potential evaluation inconsistencies.
No computational cost or latency analysis for comparing architectures.
Does not address concept drift mitigation strategies beyond identifying non-stationarity as an open problem.
remember_this: Most deep learning forecasting methods cannot provide prediction confidence intervals, except Deep Gaussian Processes.
Vanilla RNNs fail on long-term dependencies due to vanishing gradients; LSTM and GRU gated cells partially mitigate this.
PatchTST segments input into local patches processed independently, achieving competitive long-term forecasting performance.
Stationarity assumption violations cause concept drift leading to dramatic prediction accuracy decreases.
GANs and Diffusion Models represent new generative paradigms for probabilistic time series forecasting.
